title: Prefix of the unary append block
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,N,j\in\mathbb{N}$ with $j\le a+1$, and consider a base configuration on an input word $x$ of schedule symbols. Start the schedule machine in append phase $0$, with the binary-budget head at $b$, the unary-counter head at $N+1$, and the guide head at $g$; let the binary-budget tape be $\beta$, the guide tape be $\gamma$, and the unary-counter tape have an origin marker at $0$, unit markers at $1,\ldots,N$, and blanks elsewhere. After exactly $j$ steps, the state is append phase $j$, the unary-counter head is at $N+j+1$, and the unary-counter tape has an origin marker at $0$, unit markers at $1,\ldots,N+j$, and blanks elsewhere. The input-head position, all clock work tapes and their head positions, the binary-budget tape and head, the guide tape and head, and the output are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
The initial configuration is the specified setup configuration in append phase $0$
The initial unary tape is the unary tape with $N$ markers
replaced:
Let $j \le a+1$, where $a$ is the padding parameter.  From a setup configuration in
append phase $0$ with unary head at cell $N+1$ over the unary tape with $N$ markers,
exactly $j$ steps reach append phase $j$ with unary head at cell $N+j+1$ over the unary
tape with $N+j$ markers; each step writes exactly one unit marker, and all other tapes
and heads are unchanged.
